conversation.text: "Uh..." The guard uneasily shifts his gaze towards you.

conversation.text: "Which Haddin?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Arthur Haddin."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Ah, the one from the American Consulate?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David stares intently at this person. Has he seen this person before?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I'm a librarian from the Frankfurt Public Library. Haddin borrowed books from the library and hasn't returned them, so I came to collect them."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We just went up to look for him; he doesn't seem to be home."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Hearing he's a librarian, walk over to strike up a conversation.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "This is really... Do you have any news about Haddin? I'm willing to offer a personal reward." The librarian looks troubled.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That's really bad. How long has he been keeping these public books?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It's been over a month—the maximum period we allow. Those books are managed quite strictly and must be retrieved." He scratches the back of his head in distress.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What books?"

conversation.speaker: player2

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What books did he borrow that you're in such a hurry to get back?" Pretend to be concerned and step forward, "Do you have a list of the books he hasn't returned? If the late fees aren't too high, we can pass on a message for you when we see him."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: It seems this person knows exactly what books Haddin borrowed; he's probably indeed a librarian.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Just some books about social structure and political theory, which might be a bit... non-mainstream for some people." He looks very uncomfortable.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "He has such tastes? Really didn't see that coming."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "If it's just to that extent, it shouldn't matter, right? This isn't East Germany." Shrugs shoulders.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Ha, it seems you understand what kind of books those are, right?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Mainstream stuff is all the same; non-mainstream things are countless. What exactly did he read?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David listens quietly on the side.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "He's not home, and none of us can go in."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Uh... just some left-leaning political books, like Herbert Marcuse's 'Culture and Revolution', and a few more extreme ones."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "How about this: could you list the books that urgently need returning? We'll pass on the message if we run into him."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew squints in confusion, as if straining to remember.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Or perhaps you could leave your contact information?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "That's a real shame. Well, if you have any news about Haddin, or help find these books, I'd be willing to offer a personal reward. I'm Simon Weiss, a librarian at the Frankfurt Library."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright." Takes out the business card matching the fake identity and exchanges contact information with this person.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: He casually writes a note listing: The Communist Manifesto, One-Dimensional Man, Culture and Revolution, Socialist Political Economy, The Power of the People, along with his contact information.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "..." Falls silent after seeing the book list. Haddin's political spectrum is way too complicated.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Has Andrew seen these books? Could it be that he threw away the right-wing books and took the left-wing ones?

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David scratches his head. This guy reads a lot.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Andrew doesn't think he saw these books on Haddin's bookshelf; otherwise, with an agent's political sensitivity, he would have noticed.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This doesn't seem to match the image of Haddin we've encountered so far.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Gets in the car and leaves.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: David reads the letters from the Soviet veterans, who were all once prisoners of war of the Germans. The letters recall their lives in the concentration camps, mentioning that Haddin asked if they had noticed any legends about "black magic," but they mostly gave negative answers. It can be noted that one reply mentions Haddin's Russian wasn't fluent, with many grammatical errors, making it hard to read.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Why would Haddin take those books? It doesn't fit the behavior of someone fleeing in a hurry."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Those books together aren't light, and they take up a lot of space."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "He might have destroyed them, or hidden them somewhere."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Why would he do that?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player5 reads the research on Siberian indigenous shamanistic worship, roughly understanding it's an anthropological study of ethnic minorities like the Buryats, Tuvans, Chukchi, etc., discussing topics like Eternal Heaven, blessings, immortality, soul rest, etc.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Or maybe he borrowed those books not for himself to read?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Then for whom? Was he in contact with any populist organizations?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Anyway, it's absurd. How did the consulate hire someone like this?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Don't they do background checks before hiring people?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "So far, Haddin's profile is that of a spy trying to find ways to prolong life, or the soul, through every possible avenue: religion, magic, science, etc."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "He must have stumbled upon some secret stuff. After all, we're looking for him too..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Maybe he really dug up something. Did the embassy people mention to us that he acted like a cancer patient?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "He always seemed to be in poor health."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: @player3 "As is widely known, the recruitment processes of most British organizations are just formalities."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison recalls:

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Recruiting people isn't even as good as the Irish mob."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Ahem."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "At least the Irish know how to do background checks."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So, has his lifespan been successfully extended now? Chasing a dead man would be pointless."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "If he dies, will our files come back?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Finding a corpse might be easier, and it would give us something to report to headquarters. But if he really discovered something after all that research, that could be problematic."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "As a spy who had never been exposed and had been steadily providing intelligence for a long time, the Soviets had no reason to eliminate him rashly. Based on the current clues, we can only infer that Haddin's investigation to extend his life touched upon some secret, leading to him being silenced."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Frankfurt City Prosecutor's Office and Police Department are both located around Justice Square. The journey is uneventful, and you safely enter the prosecutor's office.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright, it might not necessarily be an organization; it could be a person's name, a place name, or just a codename."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The receptionist at the front desk asks formulaically.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We heard your office recently held a lecture on Nazi-era law?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We'd like to see Prosecutor Redmann. Please inform him that Mr. Kissinger's legal team is here to visit."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Ah? Alright." The receptionist picks up the phone to confirm.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Anyway, we go upstairs to find him.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You arrive on the third floor and find Redmann's office by the signs on each door. But before you can knock, you can faintly hear arguing inside.

conversation.speaker: player3

conversation.text: <player3>'s Listen check result:

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: <Male> "...This photo is the only clue. If we hold off any longer and the police find out, you know how furious they'll be?"

conversation.text: She pauses for a moment upon seeing you, then nods and says, "Good afternoon, the Prosecutor can see you now." Then she walks past you and leaves the office.

conversation.text: Do we know who Bonn is?

conversation.text: Enter the office, looking at your collaborator.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Knock politely before entering. "Good afternoon, Mr. Redmann. Mr. Kissinger's legal team sends their regards."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Redmann quickly walks over to shake your hands.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David shakes his hand and sits down.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Then leans out to confirm no one is in the nearby hallway and closes the door.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Nods slightly with approval, then puts away the detector. "Your professionalism is commendable. To be brief, we are here primarily to investigate a Foreign Ministry employee named Haddin. The clues we have indicate he previously attended an internal lecture at your office—the topic was the abuse of punishments during the Nazi era. We hope to obtain more related information from you, such as how he obtained tickets to the internal lecture."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haddin! What a coincidence!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David narrows his eyes, scrutinizing Redmann's expression. Is it fear? Anger? Shock? Or does he have some other relationship with Haddin?

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Oh, it seems you also have some information related to him. I don't think this is necessarily a coincidence," he said with a professional smile.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Ha, then please take a look at this case file first. Haddin is currently involved in a murder case. Perhaps you can gain some inspiration from it."
